meta.title: TMP-oracle-route-lookup Oracle route lookup
meta.subject: Oracle type lookup while a hospital database is in use
meta.author: LIS Team

slides.headline:
Oracle lookup stays on Oracle
while hospital work continues
slides.lede: Patient sync checks Sybase versus PostgreSQL by reading loe_control. That read currently follows the hospital route, so Oracle refuses it.
slides.notes: Patient sync already has the hospital database open. The Sybase-or-PostgreSQL check then asks Oracle on that same route, and Oracle refuses it.

slides.title: The type check fails, and the failure sticks

steps.title: Hospital database is already selected
steps.body: Patient sync has started work on the hospital Sybase or PostgreSQL database.

steps.title: The type check uses that same route
steps.body: The read of loe_control goes to Oracle, but the route is still the hospital.

steps.title: The miss is stored as PostgreSQL
steps.body: Later messages skip the check. A Sybase hospital keeps characters it cannot store.

callout.text: One failed lookup is saved as PostgreSQL, so the next messages never ask Oracle again.

slides.notes: The cache is the part that hurts. One miss is stored as PostgreSQL, so later messages never ask Oracle again. Chinese characters then stay in a message for a Sybase hospital.

slides.title: The hospital route stays put during the Oracle read

left.label: Today
left.title: Oracle is asked on the hospital route
points: After: the miss is saved as PostgreSQL

right.label: Proposed
right.title: Oracle reads its own connection
points: Route: hospital work stays where it is
Result: loe_control is read on Oracle
After: Oracle down means Sybase, unsaved

slides.notes: We do not point the whole thread at Oracle. That would commit hospital work already done. Only the Oracle read uses the Oracle connection.

slides.title: Patient sync code stays as it is

cards.title: The Oracle read succeeds
cards.body: loe_control is read on the Oracle connection even while the hospital database is selected.

cards.title: Hospital work stays open
cards.body: The hospital transaction is not switched to Oracle, so work already done is not committed early.

cards.title: Oracle down means Sybase
cards.body: This call is treated as Sybase. That answer is not saved, so the next call can ask Oracle again.

slides.notes: lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc still calls the same check. The library changes underneath it.

slides.title: Ship the library and leave config alone

cards.title: New data-source build
cards.body: Services take the fix by depending on the new library build.

cards.title: No config change
cards.body: JDBC settings stay as they are in DEVQA, SIT, and PROD.

cards.title: Patient sync only rebuilds
cards.body: lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc rebuilds to take the library. Its own source stays the same.

slides.notes: DEVQA, SIT, and PROD keep the same JDBC settings. What changes is the library binary.

slides.title: Put the previous library back

cards.title: Redeploy and restart
cards.body: Put the previous data-source build back on the affected service and restart it.

cards.title: Watch for the old warning
cards.body: On a Sybase hospital, the log should again say defaulting to PostgreSQL.

cards.title: Clear a wrong saved answer
cards.body: DELETE /api/clearCachedDBConn/{hospital}/{lab} drops one cached type check.

slides.notes: You know the rollback worked when that old warning is back on a Sybase hospital.

slides.title: Two questions before we build

asks.q: Is LOE / lab 1 / LOE_DB the only Oracle database?
asks.why: The read will use that connection unless the thread is already on Oracle.

asks.q: If a distributed transaction is already open, may this Oracle read join it?
asks.why: Hospital work will not be committed early. Distributed transactions are otherwise unchanged.

slides.notes: The first question is whether a second Oracle database is registered. The second is enlistment only. We are not redesigning distributed transactions.

slides.headline: Q&A
slides.body: Patient sync source does not change. If Oracle is down, this call is Sybase and that answer is not saved.
slides.notes: Likely questions: does patient sync source change (no), and what happens when Oracle is down (this call is Sybase, and that answer is not saved).

slides.headline: Agree the Oracle read, then build the library
slides.note: No schema change. No config change.
